summary: Lupin's quarterly sales rose 14% to INR 7,786 crore (INR 77,855 Mn) in Q2 FY2027 versus last year.
Profit (PAT) fell 22.2% year on year to INR 11,553 Mn, and EBITDA margin dropped to 27.9% from 35.6%.
U.S. sales grew 9.3% to INR 30,202 Mn, and the company got 4 ANDA approvals in the quarter.
R&D spend was 7.9% of sales and capex was INR 2,230 Mn; the company reports net cash of INR 33,490 Mn.
Management says it is mindful of near-term challenges but confident about long-term growth; no numeric targets were given.

story.what_it_does: Lupin is a pharmaceutical company that sells generic and specialty medicines, with the US its largest market at 42% of FY26 revenue. It also sells in India, Europe and emerging markets, and is building biosimilars, injectables and respiratory products.
story.plans: Management plans 15+ ANDA filings and about 20 India launches in FY27, plus 50+ US product launches over three years. It also targets 20 complex generic launches and biosimilar filings in regulated markets by 2028, and guides FY27 to high-single-digit revenue growth and about 25% EBITDA margin.
story.moat: Lupin has a large US generics pipeline, with 429 cumulative ANDA filings, and holds gross margins around 74%. It also reports net cash and a 28.4% return on capital employed in FY26, which gives it room to invest.

scenarios.story: New US launches, biosimilars, respiratory filings and India growth offset price erosion on key products, so growth stays strong. Margins hold up better than the roughly 25% FY27 guidance.
